personalExemptionScopingNote: IT-40 Booklet 2025, page 24, Schedule 3 also grants (line 2) an exemption per dependent claimed on the federal return and (lines 4-5) additional income-gated exemptions for a filer and/or spouse age 65+ with federal AGI under $40,000. StatePersonalExemption (RetireSmartIRA/StatePersonalExemption.swift) has no dependent-count field and no income parameter at all, and a codebase grep found no dependent-count input anywhere in the app, matching Kansas's Phase 5a Task 2 finding. The Phase 5a Task 7 correction is therefore scoped to Schedule 3 line 1 only: the $1,000 single / $2,000 married filing jointly base exemption for taxpayer and spouse. The dependent exemption and the income-gated age-65 addition are NOT modelled and are not folded into either base figure. None of the scenarios in this file describe a household with dependents or a filer age 65 or older, so no expectedStateTax value here is affected by either gap.

scenarios.name: single, moderate income, flat 2.95% rate net of the personal exemption
scenarios.source: Indiana Department of Revenue, Departmental Notice #1 (R46 / 01-26, effective Jan. 1, 2026), page 2: 'For 2026, the state adjusted gross income tax rate for individuals is 2.95%.' Indiana has no state standard deduction (config stateDeduction .none is correct), but IT-40 Booklet 2025, page 24, Schedule 3 'Line 1 -- Exemptions for taxpayer, spouse': 'If you are married filing jointly, enter $2,000 on this line. All other filers* should enter $1,000 on this line.' Indiana also fully excludes federally-taxable Social Security (searched and confirmed via IN DOR 'Indiana Deductions from Income': 'Indiana allows a tax deduction for any Social Security or railroad retirement benefits included in federal adjusted gross income', consistent with the audit's socialSecurityExempt true). primaryAge 55 is under 65, so no Schedule 3 line 4/5 age-65 additional exemptions apply. Indiana taxable income = 45,000 - 1,000 (single exemption) = 44,000. Tax = 44,000 * 0.0295 = 1,298.00. No age threshold or AGI phase-out gates IN's retirement-income treatment (pensionExemption/iraWithdrawalExemption both .none per the audit), so this case and the next vary income rather than age.

scenarios.name: single, high income with IRA withdrawal and Roth conversion, flat 2.95% rate net of the personal exemption
scenarios.source: Same 2.95% rate (IN DOR Departmental Notice #1, page 2) and same $1,000 single exemption (IT-40 Booklet 2025, page 24, Schedule 3 line 1). Indiana taxable income = 130,000 - 1,000 = 129,000. Tax = 129,000 * 0.0295 = 3,805.50.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses present, moderate combined income including Social Security, flat 2.95% rate net of the doubled personal exemption
scenarios.source: This is the batch's MFJ 'both spouses present' case; IN has no age-gated retirement exclusion for either spouse to qualify for, so both are simply present. IT-40 Booklet 2025, page 24, Schedule 3 line 1: married filing jointly enters $2,000. Indiana excludes federally-taxable Social Security (same IN DOR 'Indiana Deductions from Income' source as the single cases), so state income before the exemption is 95,000 - 30,000 = 65,000; Indiana taxable income = 65,000 - 2,000 = 63,000. Tax = 63,000 * 0.0295 = 1,858.50.

scenarios.name: MFJ, highest income in the batch, flat 2.95% rate net of the doubled personal exemption
scenarios.source: Same 2.95% rate and same $2,000 MFJ exemption (IT-40 Booklet 2025, page 24, Schedule 3 line 1). Indiana taxable income = 220,000 - 2,000 = 218,000. Tax = 218,000 * 0.0295 = 6,431.00.
